How confidence is setIt follows the kind of evidence, not judgement.
  • The customer's own statement (high confidence at most): The organisation says so itself: its press release, website, annual report or a named executive on the record.
  • Regulatory or securities filing (high confidence at most): A filing by the customer or the vendor names the relationship.
  • Independent press (high confidence at most): Editorially independent reporting describes the deployment.
  • Joint announcement (medium confidence at most): A press release issued with the vendor, usually with a quote from the customer.
  • Vendor case study (medium confidence at most): The vendor's published customer story naming the organisation.
  • Vendor mention only (low confidence at most): A logo, a customer list or a passing mention by the vendor, with nothing from the customer.
  • An organisation that also holds a stake in the vendor is labelled “Investor and customer” and is never rated above medium.
  • A partnership is listed as a partner, not a customer.

Questions to ask the vendor (7)

  1. Is MOSTLY AI party to any pending or recently concluded litigation that is material to its business or to its product's intellectual property?
    Material litigation can affect a supplier's finances and its ability to deliver.
  2. Has MOSTLY AI had any security incident affecting customer data or its software supply chain in the last five years, and how was each disclosed?
    A bank needs to know how a supplier has handled past security incidents.
  3. Has MOSTLY AI lost any large or regulated customer in the last 24 months, and why?
    Loss of large customers can signal product or service problems.
  4. Have there been any unplanned executive departures or conduct findings against MOSTLY AI's leadership in the last 24 months?
    Leadership instability or misconduct can disrupt a supplier.
  5. How many people at Syntho or elsewhere now work on MOSTLY AI products, and how many of them maintain the Synthetic Data SDK?
    After the original company closed, a bank needs to know who, if anyone, staffs the product.
  6. Who are the shareholders and major investors of Syntho, the current owner of the MOSTLY AI brand?
    The investors behind the original company no longer stand behind the brand; the owner's backers are what matter now.
  7. How many MOSTLY AI staff left when the operating company closed in 2026, and how many moved to Syntho?
    The closure of the operating company implies staff losses, but none are quantified in the sources.

Timeline

  1. 2026-06-09 · acquisition MOSTLY AI
    Syntho acquires the MOSTLY AI trademark and related assets

    Syntho, a synthetic data company in Amsterdam, announced it had acquired the MOSTLY AI trademark and related assets and that the brand would continue as "MOSTLY AI, powered by Syntho". The announcement does not list the assets, give terms, or say what happens to existing customers, the hosted platform or the open-source SDK. Syntho is not a tracked vendor. Syntho (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  2. 2026-03-04 · shutdown MOSTLY AI
    MOSTLY AI's operating company ceases operations and enters liquidation

    Reported by Trending Topics on 2026-03-04: chief executive Tobias Hann said the Vienna company was ceasing operations after nearly nine years and denied a rumour that it had filed for bankruptcy; the outlet said attempts to sell the company in the second half of 2025 had not succeeded. The Austrian company register publications show dissolution and liquidation of Mostly AI Solutions MP GmbH entered on 2026-03-14, a creditor call published on 2026-03-19 naming Michael Platzer and Tobias Hann as liquidators, and deletion of the company entered on 2026-09-09.
